arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Dvoretzky argued the Twenty-First Amendment restored state powers over alcohol.
Mr. Franklin argued states have complete control over liquor distribution systems.
Mr. Phillips argued the history of alcohol regulation supports state residency rules.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Tennessee law requires a person to live in the state for one year before purchasing a liquor license. Out-of-state retailers claim this rule violates the Commerce Clause. Tennessee argues the Twenty-First Amendment grants states broad control over alcohol distribution.
